hero.heading: Kenya's Next Landmark Solar Energy Project
hero.subheading: Naresho Solar Ranches is developing a 100 MW utility-scale solar photovoltaic plant in Naresho, Kajiado County — strategically positioned within Kenya's premier renewable energy corridor, with direct access to the national high-voltage grid.

opportunityBanner.text: Subject to pre-feasibility confirmation, this Project presents a compelling opportunity with the potential to become Kenya's largest solar plant — a landmark in East Africa's clean energy transition.

about.heading: Built on Strong Foundations
paragraphs: Naresho Solar Ranches is a duly incorporated Private Limited Company (Reg. No. PVT-J616JA05), registered under Kenya's Companies Act, 2015 on 14 September 2026.

We are a purpose-built vehicle to develop, finance, and operate a 100 MW solar PV plant that will feed into Kenya's national transmission network — delivering stable, clean, and competitively priced electricity at scale.
Headquartered at Victoria Towers, Westlands, Nairobi, our team combines deep local knowledge with international-grade advisory expertise across technical, financial, and legal disciplines.

project.heading: 100 MW Naresho Solar PV Plant
project.desc: A utility-scale photovoltaic development positioned at the intersection of Kenya's best solar resource, strongest grid infrastructure, and most bankable land tenure arrangements.

details.title: Strategic Location
details.text: Naresho, Kajiado County lies within one of Kenya's highest solar irradiation zones — delivering strong, consistent solar resource profiles that support competitive energy yield assumptions and long-term generation stability.

details.title: Exceptional Grid Access
details.text: The Project is in immediate proximity to a 400 kV KETRACO transmission substation forming part of Kenya's national grid. This substation serves major grid-connected assets including the Kipeto Wind Farm (majority shareholder: Meridiam) — placing Narresho within an established institutional-grade renewable energy corridor with direct access to high-voltage transmission infrastructure.

details.title: Land & Tenure
details.text: The acting project sponsor, Mr. Anthony Timayio, together with five (5) other entrepreneurs, collectively own and control approximately 800 acres of land required for development. Landowners will grant long-term lease rights to a dedicated HoldCo, which will in turn sub-lease to the Project SPV — providing clean land governance and bankable contractual arrangements.

details.title: Corporate Governance
details.text: A dedicated HoldCo is being incorporated as the Project Sponsor to institutionalise the structure and ensure bankability. The HoldCo will hold all project assets and contractual arrangements, with clear governance and an investor-ready framework suitable for capital participation at scale.

details.title: Development Path
details.text: Development has commenced with legal, technical and financial pre-feasibility to validate land rights, confirm achievable capacity, assess interconnection configuration and establish preliminary project cost. Subject to pre-feasibility confirmation, the Project will advance into full feasibility studies including ESIA, grid interconnection study, detailed financial modelling and PPA negotiation.

kenyaContext.title: Kenya Energy Context
kenyaContext.text: Kenya has set ambitious renewable energy targets under Vision 2030 and the National Energy Policy. Solar PV is a key pillar — and the Naresho Project is positioned to make a defining contribution to the nation's clean energy future.

structure.heading: A Clean, Bankable Project Architecture
structure.desc: The Project is structured to international standards — designed to satisfy institutional lenders, development finance institutions, and equity investors.

timeline.desc: A structured, phased development programme — from pre-feasibility through to commercial operations.

why.heading: Why This Project Stands Apart
why.desc: Six compelling reasons why the Naresho Solar Ranches represents a rare and strategically superior opportunity in East Africa's energy market.

cards.title: World-Class Solar Resource
cards.text: Kajiado County receives among Kenya's highest levels of solar irradiation — delivering strong, bankable energy yield projections that underpin long-term revenue stability for investors.

cards.title: Unmatched Grid Proximity
cards.text: Immediate access to the 400 kV KETRACO substation — the same infrastructure serving the Kipeto Wind Farm — significantly reduces interconnection risk, cost, and timeline compared to greenfield alternatives.

cards.title: Bankable Land Rights
cards.text: Long-term leases from owner-occupier landowners provide the project with clear, unencumbered, and bankable land tenure — a critical de-risking factor for lenders and equity investors alike.

cards.title: Institutional-Grade Structure
cards.text: The HoldCo/SPV architecture, combined with internationally reputed advisors (Questworks, Rebel Group, Ashitiva Advocates) ensures the Project meets the governance standards required by DFIs and institutional lenders.

cards.title: Favourable Market Conditions
cards.text: Kenya's growing electricity demand, government commitment to renewable energy under Vision 2030, and an established IPP framework create a highly supportive policy and commercial environment for solar investment.

cards.title: Landmark Scale & First-Mover Advantage
cards.text: At 100 MW, this project has the potential to become Kenya's largest solar plant — offering investors the prestige, scale efficiencies, and market positioning that only a landmark project can provide.
